newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-GETTING TO SUPER BOWL A DIFFICULT CHALLENGE FOR FANS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-GETTING TO SUPER BOWL A DIFFICULT CHALLENGE FOR FANS.

text.p: Getting to the Super Bowl is proving as much as a challenge for fans as it did for the New England Patriots.

Most travel packages being offered for the January 26 Super Bowl in New Orleans include roundtrip airfare, airport transfers and lodging cost about $1,600 per person based on double occupancy -- but do not include a ticket.
Travel agents reported that upper level end zone tickets for the title game against the Green Bay Packers, which have a $250 face value, are selling for $1,100.

Massachusetts Consumer Affairs Director Michael Duffy went on the offensive Monday warning fans of the American Football Conference champions to make sure that travel packages to the 31st Super Bowl include tickets to the game.
"We've had instances in the past where travel agents have sold Super Bowl tickets, but never really had them on hand," Duffy said.
Duffy said that consumers should require at the time of purchase that the game ticket be presented or that written confirmation for the ticket be provided.
Consumers should know that "getting to the Big Easy won't be as easy as some tour operators would lead them to believe," Duffy said.

"Consumers should be wary of travel operators claiming to have Super Bowl tickets. In the majority of cases we've seen, travel operators advertise and sell package deals to which they do not have tickets," he added.
This is the Patriots' first trip to the Super Bowl in 11 years. The Packers are appearing in their first Super Bowl in 29 years.
